## Desargues Involution Theorem

::: {.unnumbered-env}
**Definition.**
Suppose cross ratios can be defined on a set $E$. If a map $f:E\to E$ is a non-identity projective map and $f(f(X))=X$ for all $X\in E$, then $f$ is called an **involution** on $E$, and $(X,f(X))$ is called an **involution pair** of $f$.
:::

::: {#lem-12point1}
Let $f:E\to E$ be a projective map. If there exist $A\neq B$ such that $f(A)=B$ and $f(B)=A$, then $f$ is an involution.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Proof
Since $f$ preserves cross ratio,
$$
(A,B;X,f(X))=(B,A;f(X),f(f(X)))=(A,B;f(f(X)),f(X)).
$$
By @thm-6point4, $f(f(X))=X$ for all $X\in E$.
:::
